subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & private endpoints (FinPay)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Tan <michael.tan@finpay.com>
Cc: Rachel Li <rachel.li@finpay.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & private endpoints (FinPay)

Hi Michael / Rachel,

Thanks again for the product + security call this morning — great context. Summary and next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

High-level ask from FinPay: connect Redwood Private so FinPay services can call the inference endpoint without traversing the public internet, with strict egress controls, IP allowlist, and mTLS-based auth for the data plane.

Recap / environment details (from our notes):
- FinPay prod VPC: prod-vpc-us-east-1 (primary CIDR 10.40.0.0/16)
- Egress NAT currently owned by infra team (NAT-GW via private subnets)
- Primary DNS: internal Route53 + split-horizon for public names
- Compliance: require mTLS for service-to-service, and audit logs retained 13 months

Proposed integration pattern we discussed (attachments include architecture diagram):
1) VPC endpoint (interface endpoint) in FinPay VPC that tunnels to Redwood Private data plane (private IP).
2) Upstream IP allowlist on Redwood side restricted to the endpoint ENIs.
3) Optional egress control: keep control plane calls over public internet (if needed), but all inference traffic should use private endpoint + mTLS.
4) DNS: either Route53 private hosted zone pointing model.redwood-internal -> endpoint IP OR use endpoint IPs + SRV records as you prefer.
5) Auth: mTLS for request-level identity + per-team API keys for rate limiting/quotas.

Immediate next steps / owners:
- FinPay infra (Michael): share the subnet IDs & security group you want the interface endpoint attached to, and whether you prefer private hosted zone mapping or static IP allowlist. (due: 2026-11-08)
- Redwood infra (Lauren): provide ENI IP ranges and mTLS cert requirements doc; confirm whether we need additional NAT rules for outbound model updates. (due: 2026-11-09)
- Redwood solutions (Jonas): draft SDK auth snippet and sample routing config for model variants + embeddings/reranker flows. (due: 2026-11-09)

Attachments: redwood-architecture-diagram.png, mutual-action-plan.xlsx, mTLS-cert-requirements.pdf

If that aligns, we can get a short engineering working session on Tuesday to do the endpoint provisioning and a quick test.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (555) 322-0198

From: Michael Tan <michael.tan@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Li <rachel.li@finpay.com>, FinPay Procurement <procurement@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & private endpoints (FinPay)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from infra:

- We'll use two private subnets in us-east-1 (10.40.32.0/24 and 10.40.33.0/24) and can attach an interface endpoint into the subnets.
- Pref: private hosted zone mapping (simpler for app config). We'll create model.redwood-internal.finpay.local that resolves to the endpoint IPs.
- Security groups: we prefer least-privileged — we'll create a dedicated sg that allows outbound TLS to the endpoint ENIs.

Question from our security/infra lead (Rachel): for mTLS, do you accept a CA-signed client cert we manage, or do you require Redwood-managed client certs? Also: what CN/SANs should the server cert present for validation?

Procurement: I've looped procurement to start a statement of work and scope for dedicated capacity. Could you provide a short quote for a 3-node baseline and the account team contact for billing?

We can do the engineering working session on Tuesday at 11am ET.

Thanks — Michael

[Attachment: FinPay-network-snapshot.pdf]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Tan <michael.tan@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T12:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & private endpoints (FinPay)

Thanks Michael — quick technical clarifications from our infra side:

- mTLS: we support both options. FinPay-managed client certs are fine as long as they chain to a CA we can trust (please share CA cert and preferred CRL/OCSP endpoints). If you prefer Redwood-managed certs, we can provision short-lived client certs via our control plane (requires a cross-account trust step).
- Server cert SANs: model.redwood-internal.finpay.local and model.redwood-internal.redwood-internal (we primarily validate by IP for the endpoint, but the SANs help in mutual verification).
- IP allowlist: we'll provide a list of ENI-assigned private IPs once the interface endpoint is provisioned. Note that ENI IPs can change with scaling — we'll add a small internal CIDR (10.90.200.0/26) as the stable source if you prefer to avoid frequent updates.
- DNS: private hosted zone is supported. You'll need to create a private hosted zone attached to your VPC and add A records pointing to the endpoint IPs; we can also provide a Route53 delegation if you prefer to manage the zone from our side.
- Egress: model artifact updates (from our model registry) may require egress to our update servers; if you'd like to block that, we can push artifacts via a secure upload flow (SCP over an approved channel) during onboarding.

Jonas will attach a short SDK snippet for mTLS auth and an example embedding/reranker call pattern that shows how to pin routing to a dedicated capacity pool.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Tan <michael.tan@finpay.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & private endpoints (FinPay)

Hey team — attaching the SDK snippets inline for quick copy/paste and a small sample of how to call embeddings + reranker with structured output and tool-calling safely over mTLS.

--- SDK (python) mTLS example ---
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED", mtls_cert=("/path/to/client.crt", "/path/to/client.key"), base_url="https://model.redwood-internal.finpay.local")

# embeddings + reranker flow (high-level)
emb = client.embeddings.create(model="semi-structured-embed-001", input=["doc text"])
ranks = client.reranker.score(model="matching-ranker-1", query="invoice 1234", candidates=emb)

# structured output/tool calling note:
# If you use function/tool calling, we recommend running the tool-execution service in your VPC and exposing a secured webhook reachable from the Redwood Private endpoint. Responses should be JSON and we validate them against the model's schema on our side.

Operational notes:
- Keep API keys scoped to team-level and rotate monthly.
- For high-throughput embedding pipelines, enable batching (we can provide optimal batch sizes based on observed token distribution).
- We'll provision a canary endpoint first (single node) so you can validate connectivity, DNS, and mTLS before we roll to dedicated capacity.

Happy to jump in on Tuesday's session to walk through the endpoint test.

Thanks — Jonas

--

Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
